correctness.rationale: Assume near freeness. Gałecka's exact syzygy bounds force mdr=4, whence the nearly-free Tjurina formula gives tau=47; Bézout gives n+2t+3s=35 so s+t=12,n=t-1. Gałecka Proposition 4.4 yields t≤4. Decomposing s=u+v and counting conic incidences of seven lines yields u≥5. Hirzebruch 1985 Section 6 Eq. (9), with verified t7=t6=t5=0 for the seven-line subarrangement, bounds 9u+4v≤56, but 9u+4v=4(12−t)+5u≥57. All assumptions, local multiplicities, quantifiers and formula constants were checked. The packaged standard-library verifier reproduces zero feasible integer incidence profiles; it is not the proof of the two external inequalities.

RESULT.md complete obstruction
value.rationale: Degree nine with these three singularity types was explicitly left open in the motivating 2022 classification. This is not an arbitrary small subcase: one conic with seven lines is the structurally simplest nonlinear-component decomposition of degree nine, and removing it reduces the open classification to configurations involving multiple conics. The argument introduces a useful incidence mechanism: combine an inequality for the whole conic–line arrangement with the stronger line-only Hirzebruch inequality; it eliminates all remaining compatible weak combinatorics. This is a complete natural partial classification, not only a necessary condition or a computed witness.
risks: No claim of resolution for degree-nine arrangements containing two or more conics.
